contexts.text: The conjunction of spiritual good with its truth is signified by the ploughman reaching the reaper (). See Plough, at AE 376:6.
To sow and not to reap () = to be instructed in the truths of faith, but without increase.
The Angels who are the reapers () = truths from the Lord (which separate, AE 911:6.).
A sickle = the Divine truth of the Word... and hence to reap (), which is done with a sickle, = to put an end to the state of the Church, and to execute the Judgment. AR 645., Illustrated.
The earth was reaped () = the end of the Church because there is no longer any Divine truth in it. ( = that the Church was devastated. AE 912.)
To sow and to reap () = the implantation of good, and its reception.
Thrust in thy sickle, and reap, because the hour of thy reaping is come () = that it is the time for collecting the good, and for separating them from the evil, because it is the end of the Church.

He who reapeth receiveth reward, and gathereth fruit unto life eternal; for in this is the word, true, that it is one who soweth and another who reapeth; I sent you to reap that on which ye have not laboured... ()... To teach those who will be of the New Church... is signified by to reap. That it is not themselves who teach, thus who collect and congregate, but the Lord, ... is meant by there is one who soweth and another who reapeth... others have laboured, and ye have entered into their labour (for those whom the disciples converted to the Church had been prepared to receive by the Lord through the Angels, that is, through Divine truths from the Word).
